name: compose-db-admin-port-on-all-interfaces
task_triggers: exposing a database or admin port
attack_scenario: A Redis (6379) or Mongo (27017) bound to 0.0.0.0 with no auth is trivially discovered by internet scanners and read/dumped, or used to write keys/webshells; port 2375 exposes the Docker API directly for full host takeover.
negative_test_hint: start the stack and attempt to reach the database from an external interface, asserting no "0.0.0.0:5432" style binding exists and the connection is refused

exemplar.explanation: Explicitly binding a database or infra-management port (Postgres, MySQL, Redis, Mongo, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ mgmt, Docker API, etc.) to 0.0.0.0 publishes it on every host interface, exposing an unauthenticated or default-credential backend to the LAN or internet. The pattern matches only when the container-side port is a known backend port and word-anchors it, so app ports (0.0.0.0:8080:8080) and near-miss ports (54320, 63790) are not flagged.
